statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 futures have been halted since Friday's 21:00Z settlement, so there is no current price path to score. Friday's inside-range close, a rotational two-way session, a VIX of 14.87 and a 10-year that retraced off its 19-year intraday high keep Tail in the low band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping stays at EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. One window is flagged: the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where an unpriced weekend set - a rejected Hormuz reopening plan, a reported post-midterm strike timeline and a widened financial-isolation campaign - meets the thinnest liquidity of the week.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 6; a 19-year-high yield that closed off its extreme and a deferred strike timeline frame the 22:00Z reopen
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have not traded since Friday 25 September settled at 21:00Z, so this assessment contains no live price-path evidence and says so explicitly. The newest verified tape remains Friday's session: front NQ futures settled at 30,889.25, up 0.40%, inside a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range, while the cash Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 daily range and about 0.53% below the 30,770.63 52-week high. The VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 against a 13.38-35.30 52-week range. The S&P 500 closed at 7,743.41 (+0.51%), the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72 (+0.48%) and the Dow at 51,828.62 (+0.93%), delivering weekly gains for all three major indexes, with the Nasdaq about 3.2% higher on the week.

The most informative new evidence this run is in the driver asset rather than in equities. The 10-year Treasury yield traded to 5.233% intraday on Friday, characterised in current reporting as its highest level since 2007, and then closed back near 5.167%. A driver that prints a 19-year extreme and retracts from it is mean reversion functioning, not failing, and that materially constrains the case for a pathological equity path. The 2-year stands at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47% in the latest H.15 release for 24 September, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.88%. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point in mid-September and signalled another increase before year-end, with market pricing above 60% for a further hike at the October meeting. Equities absorbed that bond move partly because oil eased: WTI fell to roughly $92 a barrel and is about 7.4% lower on the week on Hormuz diplomacy optimism. Brent quotes conflict across feeds, below $98 in one Friday wrap and near $105 on another current feed, and that unresolved conflict caps Confidence rather than raising Tail.

Friday's internals remain the clearest evidence against a one-way basket. Delayed latest-session context shows Technology +0.85% against Communication Services -0.58%, with Semiconductor Equipment & Materials +1.76%, Semiconductors +0.56% and Software - Infrastructure +1.19% against Software - Application -0.50%. Megacap dispersion was wide in the same delayed set, with Microsoft +3.66% against Meta -3.33%, and within semis Qualcomm +3.97% against Intel -3.45%. A rotational session in which leadership changed hands while the index still closed higher is mean reversion working. That context is labelled non-real-time, its source as-of is not provided, the shared collector payload read this run is roughly 4.6 hours old with collectionStatus partial and its futures and calendar sections unavailable, and none of it can establish current NQ structure.

Three weekend developments arrived while the market was shut and therefore remain unpriced. First, Washington rejected Tehran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and Wall Street Journal reporting says the President expects bombing of Iran to resume only after the November midterm elections, with officials describing reluctance to restart major combat operations in the near term; a deferred timeline caps near-term discontinuity risk rather than raising it. Second, the Treasury Secretary described a coordinated isolation campaign in which Turkey and Oman halted incoming Mahan Air flights, the UAE suspended all Iranian airline flights, the UAE central bank blocked transactions with Bank Melli and Turkey revoked Bank Mellat's licence - a financial rather than military escalation. Third, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister called for UN protection of shipping routes while the Houthis claimed strikes on Riyadh and Aramco facilities and the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two drones aimed at the capital; the launches were intercepted rather than landing. The US Energy Secretary put Hormuz oil flows at almost 13 million barrels a day with a recent peak above 20 million, and 146 countries were reported to have condemned attacks on civilian shipping. All three strands raise Stress and cap Confidence rather than Tail. The single flagged window is the CME Globex reopen from 22:00Z on 27 September, where that unpriced set meets the thinnest liquidity of the week. Tail would only leave the low band on observed evidence after the reopen: shallow or absent pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or price holding near a session extreme.

Every hour carries a published Claude assessment. Tail eased from 8 to 6 as Friday's inside-range close and declining implied volatility aged without contradiction, Stress rose from 46 to 56 on the rate and Gulf backdrop, and Confidence drifted from 84 down to 70 as price evidence aged. No hour in the window recorded persistent one-way structure or a failed retracement sequence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are almost entirely a closed market: CME Globex equity-index futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 27 September, the seventeenth slot of this forecast. Conditional Tail therefore eases to 5 through the dead hours, ramps back toward 11 as the reopen approaches, peaks at 18 in the reopen hour, then eases to 15, 13, 12, 11, 10 and 9 as live discovery resumes. Stress runs between 54 and 61 on a 10-year that printed a 19-year high at 5.233% before closing near 5.167%, a 30-year at 5.47%, better-than-60% odds of an October Fed hike, a rejected seven-day Hormuz reopening plan, a reported post-midterm strike timeline, a widened financial-isolation campaign and intercepted Houthi launches at Saudi targets. Confidence bottoms at 62 in the last closed hours before recovering to 77 once roughly six hours of live tape exist. Every slot maps to EA_ON, and the only flagged window is 22:00Z to 23:59Z.
